_note: uv sync --extra crafter (crafter-gym, gym/crafter/, pulls crafter), then pip install --force-reinstall 'crafter @ git+https://github.com/chengfanbrain/crafter.git@deterministic' -- a fork of 1.8.3 whose single change is that a seed plus an action list replays exactly (see _state_note). Plain PyPI crafter runs this config fine and plays identically to a subject, but its blocks cannot be replayed, so a model cannot be given the same episode. This is the paradigm's level 4 (survival), which is stock crafter: hostiles on, health/food/drink/energy decay, death ends the episode, nothing hidden from the HUD. Levels 1-3 freeze or remove parts of that and belong in a gymnasium.Wrapper shipped with the env, not here: an adapter that added them would stop humans and models from playing the same game.
_keys_note: Crafter's Discrete(17) map is 0=noop, 1=move_left, 2=move_right, 3=move_up, 4=move_down, 5=do, 6=sleep, 7=place_stone, 8=place_table, 9=place_furnace, 10=place_plant, 11=make_wood_pickaxe, 12=make_stone_pickaxe, 13=make_iron_pickaxe, 14=make_wood_sword, 15=make_stone_sword, 16=make_iron_sword. All 17 are bound here, so every action is reachable; '' is the frame with no key held, which crafter calls noop. Arrows + SPACE + S are the six keys the scanner paradigm teaches, and R/T/F/P and 1-6 are the letters crafter's own run_gui.py uses for the other ten. For a button box with fewer buttons use crafter__crafter_menu.json rather than cutting this list, which would put the tech tree above 'collect wood' out of reach. Keep the message Controls text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_pacing_note: fps is the env step rate, so it sets how fast the survival clock runs against scanner time. Crafter's own interactive player defaults to 5 (run_gui.py, --fps), which is the only human-play cadence the engine documents; 2.5 is the scanner setting, chosen deliberately: 400 ms a decision instead of 200 ms, which is enough time to read the HUD and pick one of 17 actions under button-box constraints, at the cost of halving the game clock so a 300 s block covers half the survival day. turn_based is false on purpose: with hostiles and homeostatic decay, freezing the world until the subject presses a key would remove the survival pressure and decouple game time from scanner time. latched_keys makes each frame prefer a fresh keydown over the held-key poll, so a tap shorter than one frame is not dropped, which is what run_gui.py does. One action per frame, last press wins.
_score_note: show_score draws the achievement count in the HUD strip above the frame, which crafter's own HUD does not show. It covers no game pixel and reports only values already in info['achievements'], so the model harness can be given the same scalar; if a model is ever evaluated without it, say so, because that is a difference in what the two players can see. The count is shown rather than the block's cumulative reward, which is the same quantity written less legibly: crafter pays +1 per first unlock and (health - last_health)/10 per step, and the health terms telescope to at most -0.9 over an episode.
_cue_note: cues turns on the three synthesized sounds in the adapter, because crafter itself ships none and three outcomes are otherwise invisible in the bore: a blow that landed on a creature without killing it (five bare-handed presses for a zombie), a press the engine refused (no pickaxe for that rock, no table in reach), and a press the rig dropped. score > hit > blocked, at most one a frame, since audio output queues rather than mixes. The cue is decided from the state the engine is about to act on, not by diffing state afterwards, which cannot see a non-lethal blow at all; it is exact because the player updates first every step, and it reads crafter's own collect/place/make tables without touching the world or its RNG. Collecting grass stays silent on purpose: data.yaml gives it probability 0.1, so a press that yields nothing is a failed roll, not a refusal. cue_overlay writes the same feedback as a field in the HUD strip, and it is off here deliberately: the subject has already heard the cue, so the field only repeats it, and a word appearing above the frame pulls the eyes off it between presses. The agent harness turns it on for itself, since a policy cannot hear a sound and would otherwise be told less than the subject was. The columns hit / no_effect / cue / target land in the npz however both flags are set.
_state_note: state_stride 25 = one pickled savestate every 10 s at 2.5 fps, counted per episode. At size 384 a state is 2.3 MB and ~3 ms to write or read, but only 0.16 MB of that is the game: the rest is the observation space's constant bounds and the cached frame, and zlib leaves ~57 KB an anchor inside the npz. A measured 300 s block on the fork held 32 anchors, 76 MB raw and 1.8 MB in the compressed npz, and every one of them restored and then played its episode out frame-for-frame identically to the seed replay: that is what makes an anchor a branch point a model can be rolled out from. log_frames stores the displayed pixels too, zlib'd per frame (7.4 KB median in daylight; crafter mixes per-pixel noise into the view at night, so the 107 night frames of that block reached a median 185 KB and 217 KB at the worst, and the block came to 750 frames / 22.5 MB of pixels in a 22.5 MB npz). Frames are kept even though the fork replays exactly, because they are the record that does not depend on whoever opens the block later having the fork installed. On stock crafter they are the only record: it rebalances creatures every tenth step by iterating a Python set of objects, so the despawn choice follows object id() and two runs of the same seed and actions diverge (measured 2026-09-28 across two PYTHONHASHSEEDs: step 30 of a 225-action episode, which then ended a step early; a restored anchor is worse off still, since unpickling renumbers every object). Terrain is identical either way; creatures are not.
_size_note: size 384 is an integer half of the 768-pixel display height. display.draw_frame scales unfiltered, so a fractional factor smears crafter's pixel art, and the counters crafter draws into the bottom two of its nine tile rows are what suffers first. length 0 removes crafter's own 10000-step cap: the block is bounded by its duration, so every ending is a real death.
